Acts 2:42–47 describes the early Christian community formed after Pentecost.
Refuge plans to launch later this year, contingent on the evolution of the COVID situation.
This early Christian community was defined by devotion to the apostles’ teachings, fellowship, and mission.
The speaker encourages viewers to visit the connections page in the video description.
The speaker wants to learn more about attendees and how to serve and pray for them during the pandemic.
Scripture is written for believers but primarily about Jesus, not about human failure.
Engaging Scripture through the lens of the gospel leads to transformation, not condemnation.
Praying Scripture involves thanksgiving, confession, repentance, and worship.
Attending a community group requires active participation and vulnerability.

Loneliness in modern American culture stems from cultural values like individualism and materialism.

Believers are expected to actively participate in evangelism and disciple-making as part of their identity.
Community groups provide essential relational safety and accountability for spiritual growth.
The Holy Spirit enables believers to live out biblical virtues beyond their natural capacity.
Audiences value authenticity and vulnerability more than performance or perfection in religious expression.
Divine action (e.g., 'the Lord adding to their number') depends on communal faithfulness and witness.
